visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A massive white projection screen displays a stylized, animated Mount Fuji. A woman in a checkered shirt and khaki pants sits on a red bench in the foreground, watching as the projection transitions from snowy white to vibrant, multi-colored floral patterns across the mountain. The setting is a spacious, dimly lit exhibition hall with visible wooden rafters. (2) The camera pans across large wall displays featuring classic Japanese Ukiyo-e prints, including high-detail portraits of Kabuki actors with dramatic facial expressions and the famous "Great Wave off Kanagawa." Detailed text descriptions in Chinese are printed alongside the art. The lighting is focused and warm, highlighting the textures of the prints against the dark walls. (3) In an interactive zone, a woman pushes through vertical curtain strips that display a panoramic, animated projection of a traditional Japanese riverside landscape with figures. The environment feels immersive as the projection wraps around the room's corner. The floor is grey and neutral, keeping focus on the glowing interactive elements. (4) A 360-degree projection room shows life-sized women in colorful, traditional kimonos standing among falling cherry blossom petals. A woman stands captivated in the center, her silhouette backlit by the bright screens. The colors are highly saturated pinks and blues, and the floor reflects the projected light. (5) Close-up shots show game-like installations. A woman uses a wooden plunger on a pinball-style game made of wood with colorful holes, and then uses a toy rod to 'fish' for paper illustrations from a projected pond on the floor. These activities are located in a well-lit, interactive corner of the exhibition. (6) A demonstration of a multi-stage stamping process is shown. Hands press a series of red plastic stamps onto a white card, each layer adding a different color or detail to eventually reveal a complex, finished replica of the Hokusai wave. The focus is tight on the card and the stamping motion. (7) A woman stands before a large black-and-white digital screen. As she touches the surface, colorful elements like red birds and pink cherry blossoms bloom and fly across the display, showing real-time interactive responses. The lighting is low to emphasize the brightness of the interactive screen.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) Background music begins with an upbeat, bright electronic-pop melody featuring a prominent synthesizer lead and a steady percussive beat. The acoustic space is clean, resembling a post-produced studio track. A soft percussive thud occurs as the camera switches from the mountain projection to the wall portraits. (2) As the viewer enters the interactive curtain area, a synthesized "whoosh" sound effect layers over the music to accentuate the motion. The BGM remains constant in tempo and energy. The soundstage feels wide, mirroring the expansive visual environment of the exhibition hall. (3) During the game segment, clear incidental sounds of wooden impacts from the pinball game and soft rustling are audible. These are mixed to be distinctive without overpowering the cheerful background music. The beat of the track keeps a consistent 105 BPM rhythm throughout this phase. (4) Rhythmic percussive thumps are heard as the stamp is pressed onto the paper card, marking each layer of the image creation. The music continues its loop with no variations in pitch or intensity. The acoustic clarity of the stamping sound indicates a close-up recording or well-placed microphone. (5) A high-pitched, magical "sparkle" or "chime" sound effect triggers as the woman touches the interactive wall, perfectly synchronized with the digital flowers blooming. This sound effect is sharp and bright, contrasting with the mid-range synth melody of the background music. The video concludes as the music fades slightly.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a promotional showcase for a Japanese 'Moving Ukiyo-e' digital art exhibition. It aims to attract visitors by highlighting the visual spectacle of massive projections, the nostalgia of traditional prints, and the interactive, family-friendly activities like games and stamping.
